Leaders of eight Nordic and Baltic countries—Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia—issued a joint statement following a phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, reaffirming their commitment to continue supplying weapons to Ukraine and strengthening Europe's defense to deter further Russian aggression. The leaders pledged to maintain and expand sanctions and economic measures against Russia as long as the war continues. They highlighted Ukraine’s consistent willingness to pursue peace, including its readiness for negotiations and work on a peace plan proposed by the U.S., while noting that Russia has not taken any steps toward ceasefire or peace efforts, instead continuing attacks on Ukrainian civilians and infrastructure. Western leaders called for revisions to the U.S. 'peace plan' under President Donald Trump, which reportedly includes territorial concessions by Ukraine, financial support for reconstruction, gradual lifting of sanctions on Russia, and a long-term economic agreement between Moscow and Washington. The U.S. gave Ukraine until November 27, 2025, to accept the plan, threatening to halt weapons deliveries and intelligence sharing if rejected. The plan is set to be discussed at a meeting on November 23, 2025, in Geneva, involving EU, U.S., and Ukrainian representatives, including Andriy Yermak (head of the President’s Office), Rustem Umerov (Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council), Kyrylo Budanov (Head of the Ukrainian General Staff), and Serhiy Kyslytsya (Deputy Foreign Minister). The joint statement was also signed by leaders of Germany, the UK, Ireland, Spain, Italy, Canada, the Netherlands, France, Japan, and by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa.
